Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-slack-medium-0012", "row_sha256": "5abf3cdbf5b19af794f2be0790bb10c1b2cbbf2a45eaa0c8955470926ef946cc", "mode": "/slack", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Fix grammar, punctuation, and shorthand with minimal edits. Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "hey folks, quick update on the lending shelf: we moved it beside the front desk on monday, and there are 18 games on it now, up from 11 last month. the new labels show the player count and usual play time, which has cut down on questions at pickup. folks can still borrow one game at a time for up to two weeks; the sign-up sheet is in the blue folder under the shelf.

we've had 9 returns so far this week, and 7 came back with all the pieces. two boxes were missing cards, so i put those games in the repair bin and added a note to the sheet. please check the box contents before you take a game, and mark any missing pieces when you return it.

one caveat: the shelf seems useful for regulars, but we only have one month of sign-out notes, and we don't know yet whether the new location is bringing in more first-time borrowers. if the front desk gets busy during the evening rush, we'll move the shelf back to the side room; for now, we're keeping it there through the end of the month.", "output": "Hey folks, quick update on the lending shelf: We moved it beside the front desk on Monday, and there are 18 games on it now, up from 11 last month. The new labels show the player count and usual play time, which has cut down on questions at pickup. Folks can still borrow one game at a time for up to two weeks; the sign-up sheet is in the blue folder under the shelf.

We've had 9 returns so far this week, and 7 came back with all the pieces. Two boxes were missing cards, so I put those games in the repair bin and added a note to the sheet. Please check the box contents before you take a game, and mark any missing pieces when you return it.

One caveat: The shelf seems useful for regulars, but we only have one month of sign-out notes, and we don't know yet whether the new location is bringing in more first-time borrowers. If the front desk gets busy during the evening rush, we'll move the shelf back to the side room; for now, we're keeping it there through the end of the month."}]
